nesnd_c2_italy_foundations_public_works_: Get the army's supplies under way first, and the workshops will have orders enough.
Army First in Line for Contracts
nesnd_c2_italy_foundations_commercial_cr: Let the merchants raise credit for the workshops. A mill opens only when someone can lend the money.
nesnd_c2_italy_foundations_local_partner: Bring the townsfolk who pay into running the schools, and their own children will have a place to study.
nesnd_c2_italy_foundations_reason: France's patronage of the Lombard Republic has given the republican cause in Italy something to lean on. But the orders for the workshops, the merchants' credit and the money for local schools must still be found by Italians themselves. The army wants military works first, the merchants want loans with a fixed term, and the townsfolk who fund the schools want a place for their own children.
nesnd_c2_italy_common_budget_fiscal_unio: Gather the taxes in one place, and common undertakings can finally be paid for.
nesnd_c2_italy_common_budget_federal_cou: Let each state keep its school money, and the schools will open on its own doorstep.
nesnd_c2_italy_common_budget_military_ac: Count army pay and the settlement of veterans among the public works as well.
nesnd_c2_italy_common_budget_reason: Before Italy can come together, someone must settle the accounts of each state's armies and taxes. The industrialists want resources pooled, local traders want to keep the money for schools, and the army puts military pay and veterans first. Whether the states bargain one by one or unite at a stroke, there is no way round the question of who controls the revenue.
nesnd_c2_hus_transport_chartered_contrac: Hand the ports and roads to the big contractors and build them with their capital.
nesnd_c2_hus_transport_open_tenders_desc: Put the works out to open tender, so the small firms get their share of the jobs.
nesnd_c2_hus_transport_local_transport_d: Run the branch lines out to the country market towns first.
nesnd_c2_hus_transport_local_transport_p: Branch Lines to Market Towns First
nesnd_c2_hus_transport_reason: Dongqing trades across the ocean, and its ports must be linked to inland timber, ore and farm produce. The big contractors bring capital, but they bring concessions with it, and the districts they serve will come to depend on them. Smaller firms want open tenders, and the countryside wants branch lines run to its own market towns first.
nesnd_c2_hus_frontier_pasture_passage_de: Leave a path for the herds. The works must detour around the pasture routes and will go more slowly.
nesnd_c2_hus_frontier_land_compensation_: Pay a fair price for the land taken. The road will get built, but it will take longer.
Land Bought at a Fair Price
nesnd_c2_hus_frontier_frontier_garrisons: Station troops along the works, and the road will get built.
nesnd_c2_hus_frontier_reason: Railways and mines are pushing into the pastures. The blanks on the map are crossed by herds every year: the animals need water, the works need land, and the garrisons need secure roads. The herders want the routes left open, the developers press for land bought outright, and the army proposes troops to guard the works.
nesnd_c2_hus_citizenship_labour_schools_: Put the children of debt-bound families, and the workers themselves, into school.
nesnd_c2_hus_citizenship_public_accounts: Lay out every coin spent on the public works for all to see.
nesnd_c2_hus_citizenship_reason: The sons of debt-bound families have come into the workshops, and their old debts, their inherited rank and the dependence they cannot shake off have come in with them. Teachers and workers want a chance to learn; local traders want to know whose pockets the public works money went into. The argument over freedom and standing has landed in the schoolroom and the workshop.
nesnd_c2_hus_oil_oil_concessions_desc: Grant the drilling rights as concessions and let the companies sink new wells with their profits.
nesnd_c2_hus_oil_oil_royalties_desc: Keep the oil revenue where the oil comes from, and spend it on roads and schools.
nesnd_c2_hus_oil_oil_oversight_desc: Let the workers' organisations watch over the wells, and put the local assistance into schools.
nesnd_c2_hus_oil_reason: The wells have struck oil, and where the money goes has become local politics. The concession companies want to plough the profits into further expansion, the traders want the royalties kept for roads and schools, and the workers' organisations want the whole industry brought into the open under public oversight.
nesnd_c2_usm_constitution_classical_fran: Classical learning is the foundation of office. That must not be touched.
nesnd_c2_usm_constitution_practical_fran: A man who understands machines and can keep accounts deserves a road into office too.
nesnd_c2_usm_constitution_local_franchis: Give the provinces more examination places, so their sons have a chance to rise.
nesnd_c2_usm_constitution_reason: At the doors of the Assembly of Rites stand scholars versed in the classics, and beside them newcomers who understand machinery, accounts and trade. The cabinet and Six Ministries want capable men from among them, and every province wants to know whether its own sons will be chosen. How much weight goes to classical qualifications, practical experience and provincial places decides who may enter public life under the Constitution, and puts the old gentry's standing in question.
nesnd_c2_usm_schools_practical_schools_d: Add practical courses to the academies, and the teachers' salaries will be found.
nesnd_c2_usm_schools_provincial_schools_: Give the provinces more school places, so the village youth have books to read.
nesnd_c2_usm_schools_reason: The academy teachers lecture on the classics; their students want surveying, machinery and commercial learning. The students hope to learn something useful, and hope even more to qualify for the Assembly of Rites examinations. Provincial administrators have to find the money, and provincial delegates carry each province's demands for courses and places into national politics. Practical courses and provincial places are fighting over the same education budget.
nesnd_c2_usm_industry_coastal_industry_d: Put the money into the coastal works first. That is where the ports and shipping lanes are.
nesnd_c2_usm_industry_inland_industry_de: Industry cannot stop at the coast. The interior needs roads and works of its own.
nesnd_c2_usm_industry_reason: Coastal merchants set up their workshops along the ports and shipping lanes, and the inland towns hold out their hands for investment too. Machinery, labour and goods must move between provinces, yet each provincial administrator sees only his own province's taxes and building costs. Prosperity in memorials to the throne counts for nothing; only works that keep running show where the money went.
nesnd_c2_usm_distribution_commercial_emp: Concentrate the investment where trade already thrives, and put the best steel to the sharpest edge.
Trading Ports Take the Lion's Share
nesnd_c2_usm_distribution_provincial_bal: Move public funds between provinces, so that even the poor ones can afford their works.
nesnd_c2_usm_distribution_scholars_franc: Widen the qualifications for provincial delegates and let more scholars into the Assembly of Rites.
nesnd_c2_usm_distribution_reason: New works and new shipping have brought in new revenue. It can be poured back into the thriving commercial centres, or shared among the provinces for public works. The cabinet and Six Ministries plan the spending; the provincial delegates in the Assembly of Rites must answer for what their provinces paid in and what they got back. The constitutional quarrel over shares now has a fresh pot of money to fight over.
nesnd_civic_routes.1.d: The works have survived their first months and settled into everyday operation. The services and production that the money paid for are showing real results, and the long local argument over costs and returns finally has accounts to check.
nesnd_c2_retarget_desc: After the present funding term, choose another site within the current borders. Money already paid is not refunded, and the new site must prove itself again.
nesnd_c2_italy_agenda_reason: France shields the Lombard Republic, yet each Italian state still pays for its own army, schools and officials. Whether they seek unification or lasting cooperation, the Italians must first agree on where the money for common undertakings comes from and who spends it.\n\nThis [concept_journal_entry] ends if the country loses its Italian primary cultures or all its inhabited states in Italy.
nesnd_c2_hus_frontier_choose: First choose one of three courses: pasture routes, land purchase or garrisons.
nesnd_c2_hus_citizenship_choose: Choose one course: fund workers' education, or open the public works accounts.
nesnd_c2_usm_agenda_reason: The cabinet and Six Ministries propose new measures, the Assembly of Rites debates the Constitution, provincial administrators run finance and government, and provincial delegates speak for their provinces in national affairs. Academy students learn their trades while preparing for the Assembly's examinations. The more schools and industries open, the louder the quarrel over who may enter office and who must pay.
nesnd_civic_routes.10.d: A neighbouring state proposes that we share the burden of public works. Schools, local taxes and army costs would no longer be fine words in speeches about unity: each country would pay from its own treasury and get the work done on its own soil. The proposal leaves both governments and both territories untouched.
nesnd_civic_routes.10.a: Each pays its share, and what we agreed gets done.
nesnd_civic_routes.10.b: Schools and local services come first.
nesnd_civic_routes.10.c: We will not sign up to this bill.
nesnd_civic_routes.11.d: The other side will cooperate, on condition that the money goes to schools and local services rather than military supply. If we agree, both countries fund these undertakings, each running the services within its own borders.
nesnd_civic_routes.11.a: Schools first, then. So be it.
nesnd_civic_routes.12.d: The states could not agree on this term's public obligations. Schools, taxes and army costs remain each state's own business.
nesnd_civic_routes.13.d: Both countries have kept their word, each finding the money and the people for its schools, administration or military supply. Having made cooperation work once, the next round of talks should come easier.
nesnd_civic_routes.13.a: Carry on as we have begun.
nesnd_c2_usm_west_fail: Western provincial integration has failed. The schools and industries we already run will be kept going.
je_risorgimento_reason: Each Italian state has its own government, army and foreign ties. The Lombard Republic has France at its back, and republicans, dynasties and local purse-holders all want to point the way to unity. Some want a single Italy; others want no more than lasting cooperation on public obligations.
italian_unification.6.d: Political mobilisation has stirred up local politics across Italy. Old republics and newly organised republicans are courting allies, but nothing is settled: not how to share army costs, not how to raise taxes, not how to choose representatives.
italian_unification.10.d: Everyone is arguing over Italy's future: in the schools, in the barracks, in the councils of every state. Unity need not mean a quarrel with France; but how to divide the revenue, and who has the right to sit in council, are questions French protection cannot answer for the Italians.
nesnd_civic_routes.30.d: Slavery is abolished, and assembly and speech are protected by law. A debt bond can no longer rule a person's whole life as it once did. But what the registration order left behind will not vanish overnight: who may study, who may take up which trade, who counts as what — the republic will have to fight over each in turn.
nesnd_civic_routes.40.d: The southern government has asked Duan Jingchuan to join its discussions on academy curricula and places. Sichuan is independent now; Nanjing can no longer summon a man with a provincial order as it once did. Whether he goes is for us to decide.
nesnd_civic_routes.41.d: Sichuan has agreed to the teacher exchange. The academies on both sides can keep up regular contact on curricula and places, while each runs its own schools. Qualification for the Assembly of Rites still depends on the southern government's own examinations and constitutional procedures.
nesnd_ui_c2_no_active_plan_tt: No plan has been chosen for this undertaking
nesnd_ui_c2_plan_chosen_tt: A plan has been chosen for this undertaking
